question: What is the least number of soldiers that can stand in rows of 11, 12 and 16 with none left over, and can also stand in a square (as many rows as in each row)?

question: Two gear wheels with 21 and 49 teeth turn together. A marked tooth of each is touching now. After how many complete turns of the smaller wheel will the two marked teeth touch again?
solution: They meet again when the number of teeth passed is a multiple of both 21 and 49: LCM(21, 49) = 147 teeth. The smaller wheel then makes 147 ÷ 21 = 7 turns.

question: When the eggs in a basket are counted in 6s, 8s and 9s, 2 are left over each time, but when they are counted in 13s none is left over. What is the least number of eggs in the basket?
solution: The number is 72k + 2 (LCM(6, 8, 9) = 72). Try k = 1, 2, ...: 74 ÷ 13 leaves 9; 146 ÷ 13 leaves 3; 218 ÷ 13 leaves 10; 290 ÷ 13 leaves 4; 362 ÷ 13 leaves 11; 434 ÷ 13 leaves 5; 506 ÷ 13 leaves 12; 578 ÷ 13 leaves 6; 650 ÷ 13 is exact. Least = 650.

question: In an exam 96 students take Hindi, 256 take English and 304 take Maths. Every room must seat the same number of students, all taking the same subject. What is the least number of rooms needed?
solution: Fewest rooms means the most students in a room: HCF(96, 256, 304) = 16. Rooms = 96 ÷ 16 + 256 ÷ 16 + 304 ÷ 16 = 6 + 16 + 19 = 41.

question: A shopkeeper has 1176 litres, 1344 litres and 1428 litres of three kinds of juice. He fills them, without mixing, into tins of one size so that every tin is full. What is the least number of tins he needs?
